author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list answers a page below 1 with the first page
summary: Requesting the owner list, or any owner search, at a page numbered below 1 currently shows the error page. The owner list must answer such a request as the first page and respond with the normal listing, and a test must cover the fix.
acceptance_criteria: Given several pages of owners, when /owners is requested with page=0, then the response is HTTP 200 with the normal owner listing, not the error page.

Given any page value below 1 (0, a negative number, and the lowest integer a request can carry), when the owner list is requested, then it shows the same owners as page 1 and marks page 1 as the current page.

Given a last-name search at a page value below 1, when it runs, then the outcome matches the same search at page 1: one match opens that owner's record, several matches list the first page, and no match reports that no owner was found.
The fix is covered by a controller test that fails against the current code and passes after the fix.
non_goals: The owner list's answer for a page past the last page: left open in the PRD's Open Questions, outside the quoted request.
The owner list's answer for a page value that is not a number: left open in the PRD's Open Questions, outside the quoted request.
Changing the page size, the pagination controls, or the veterinarian directory's paging.
notes: Cause observed: the owner list subtracts one from the page number to build a zero-based page index, and the paging request rejects a negative index. That unhandled failure renders the error page. The implementer confirms this with a reproducing test first. Decision (reversible, mine): 'treats any page value below 1 as the first page' means identical to page 1 for every search outcome, including the single-match redirect. HTTP 200 applies to the multi-owner listing the owner reported. PRD edits: REQ-OWN-005 narrative clause, two Done-when bullets, Owner records edge case 4, one Open Question, and a provenance note marking REQ-OWN-005 as owner-stated. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides entry. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log. Ubiquitous language: no new domain term needed.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by the existing owner search handler: system-design.md § Contracts row OwnerController (server-rendered search with paging; REQ-OWN-005 added to its Implements cell, the only design write), and the pattern catalog's Web controller row (architecture-principles.md), whose 'binds the request' duty includes normalizing the page query parameter. Clamping the page to the first page is range handling of external input at the HTTP boundary, as security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries requires ('validate type, range, and shape before use'). It is not a domain business rule, so it adds no new controller-rule violation under architecture-principles.md § Design Validation Checklist. The PRD contract answers below-1 as page 1 rather than rejecting it, so normalization is the contract's answer. Basis: headless run, no IDE oracle. The covering code was resolved by reading OwnerController.java (processFindForm binds @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page; findPaginatedForOwnersLastName builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize); addPaginationModel sets currentPage from the raw page). That is a file read, the weaker basis compared with a symbol-resolution call.
integration_points: Entry point GET /owners (existing, not new): the page parameter binds to a request-scoped primitive int. Normalize it once at the top of processFindForm, before any use, so the Pageable, the single-match redirect, the not-found branch, and the currentPage model attribute all see the first page. The existing Owner search-form binding keeps its id/*.id disallow list unchanged; this slice adds no bound field.
Framework transport boundary: MockMvc via the existing @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class) harness, the sanctioned double per testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy.

Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): the test class's existing class-level @MockitoBean. This is a conscious framework-stub exception: @WebMvcTest loads no JPA, so a real repository is unavailable in this slice, and a hand-written double would have to implement the whole inherited JpaRepository surface. Stub findByLastNameStartingWith with the first-page Pageable matched exactly (eq(PageRequest.of(0, 5)) or an argument captor asserting page index 0), not any(Pageable), so the test proves the controller asked for page 1. Return a PageImpl with several owners and a total above the page size for the listing case, one owner for the redirect case, and an empty page for the not-found case.

risks.risk: Lowest integer page (Integer.MIN_VALUE): subtracting 1 before clamping wraps to Integer.MAX_VALUE and yields a huge offset instead of an exception, so a clamp placed after the subtraction misses it.
risks.mitigation: Clamp before any arithmetic, e.g. max(page, 1), per security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries (validate range before use). Parameterize the test over 0, -1, and Integer.MIN_VALUE as acceptance criterion 2 names.

risks.risk: Clamping only inside the pagination helper fixes the query but leaves currentPage at the raw value, which fails acceptance criterion 2 (page 1 marked current).
risks.mitigation: Normalize once at the handler entry and pass the normalized value to both helpers. The web controller binds the request before delegating (architecture-principles.md pattern catalog, Web controller row).

risks.risk: Scope creep into the identical page - 1 construction in VetController, or into the non-numeric and past-last-page cases.
risks.mitigation: All three are excluded by the prd-entry non_goals and remain open in the PRD's Open Questions. Leave VetController and type-mismatch handling untouched.

author: system-design-expert
answer: Keep the clamp where it is. Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) at the top of OwnerController.processFindForm is request binding under the Web controller row, not a business rule, and the line-5 design-block stands unchanged. No code change this round: re-run the gate and re-invoke code-quality-reviewer with this answer. Classification (now durable memory): mapping a request parameter into the range its delegate accepts counts as binding when two conditions hold. (1) The PRD states the answer for the out-of-range value; REQ-OWN-005 does for a page below 1. (2) The mapping reads the request alone, never clinic records. Where the PRD is silent, the boundary rejects the value (security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries: validate range before use, reject what the contract does not allow; checks belong at the boundary, not in the core). A check against clinic records (duplicate pet name, birth or visit date, whether a record exists) stays a business rule, and a new one in a controller is still a fresh violation. The reviewer's reading of the checklist is right for that class. The page clamp falls outside it. Alternatives rejected: a page-number value object would put a transport concern into the domain as a type the ubiquitous language does not contain, and it would add a public name for one comparison (architecture-principles.md Design Principles 2 and 5). A static normalizer matches no catalog pattern and moves the check away from the boundary it guards. The framework's Pageable resolver would change binding globally, change the handler signature, and change non-numeric handling, which the PRD leaves open. testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid already names normalization as a web-controller duty tested at the web level. It says extracting such a rule for a unit test is placement drift, so the existing MockMvc tests are the correct tests. On your third question: yes, and it is now recorded. docs/system-design.md § Package Structure carries the classification as a current-state rule with REQ-OWN-005, backed by a new ADR. That supplies the system-design.md assignment testing-principles.md line 54 already assumed. Cite both in the re-review.

memory_updates.summary: § Package Structure: new paragraph 'Request normalization is binding, not a business rule'. It states the two conditions (the PRD states the out-of-range answer; the mapping reads the request alone), the reject-when-silent default, and the clinic-records business-rule counterexample. It records OwnerController's page-below-1 normalization at handler entry [REQ-OWN-005] and says the recorded controller-rule breach neither covers nor widens to it. Links the new ADR.
